external_relations.target_title: Post-compaction: audit xtrm-ui tool rendering overhead and pi tool-call slowdown

source.description:
PROBLEM: Pi feels slow across tool calls and turn-end. We need a repeatable isolation smoke instead of judging by TUI feel. Current suspects include xtrm-ui rendering overhead, global raw extensions, and xtmux agent-state lifecycle hooks.

SCOPE: Build or document a minimal timing procedure that compares: baseline/no relevant extensions, xtrm-ui enabled, xtmux-agent-state enabled, and both enabled. Include detection for raw global extensions under ~/.pi/agent/extensions because pi list only shows packages.

SUCCESS: A command checklist or small script reports median timings for several simple bash/read/write/edit calls and turn-end latency. It must explicitly identify loaded packages and raw extension files, and include a verdict taxonomy: PASS/no evidence, SUSPECT/needs isolation, CONFIRMED/bottleneck.

NON_GOALS: Do not benchmark model latency. Do not require external services. Do not permanently disable user extensions.

CONSTRAINTS: Measurements must be cheap and reversible. Prefer env toggles or temporary extension renames over reinstalling packages. Preserve bd/security gates unless explicitly testing no-extension baseline.

VALIDATION: Run at least one local sample and record medians. Verify the smoke catches the xtmux message_update/tool_execution_start issue or proves it resolved after debounce.

OUTPUT: Script/checklist path plus sample output and recommended thresholds.
